ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0), Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 627a, Commercial Register Ordinance (CRO, SR 221.411) Arts. 3 and 3a, and the Federal Embargo Act (SR 946.211).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the UBO's country of residence and utility provider

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the foreign jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs and commercial counterparties against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Swiss SECO sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence is required for PEPs and their family and close associates under Art. 3 AMLA; ongoing monitoring is required under Art. 6 AMLA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex) and the cantonal commercial register (Handelsregister)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in an official Swiss language (German, French, Italian or Romansh) or in a Latin-script transliteration; the legal-form suffix 'AG' (or 'SA' in French/Italian) is mandatory.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written rejection, the applicant may file an appeal with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority within 30 days; further appeal may be made to the Federal Administrative Court in Bern. Applicants may also modify the name and resubmit without losing the reservation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may serve as the postal/service address, but the dietary-supplements trading licence and high-risk merchant account mandate a physical operating address; therefore a purely virtual office without commercial substance is not acceptable for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 45% annual probability of unannounced inspections in the first two years, with higher scrutiny in the e-commerce nutraceutical sector.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht), Arts. 620 et seq. and Arts. 640 and 643, governing incorporation, share capital, articles of association, and registration of an Aktiengesellschaft.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug / Commercial Register Office of Canton Zug, Switzerland
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (öffentliche Urkunde) and application for registration in the Commercial Register (Anmeldung zur Eintragung)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is CHF 100,000. The minimum cash contribution to be paid up before registration is 20% of the nominal capital, but in all cases not less than CHF 50,000, which must be credited to a blocked escrow account at a licensed Swiss bank and held for the company until the Commercial Register entry is effected.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company, a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft governed by Articles 620 et seq. of the Swiss Code of Obligations, adopts this First Board Resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the founders' subscription and payment of CHF 100,000 share capital divided into 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 par value each are accepted; the minimum paid-up sum of CHF 50,000 is deposited to the Company's blocked escrow account. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at [Address], Zug, Switzerland. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Given Name] [Surname] is appointed Sole Director and [Given Name] [Surname] is appointed Corporate Secretary, each with authority to execute all filings and open bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation and company purpose verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canton Zug Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation request for the Swiss company name ending in 'AG' and verify that the proposed corporate purpose covers online retail of dietary supplements and nutraceuticals, including cross-border e-commerce. Confirm the name does not conflict with existing registrations and obtain the official reservation confirmation.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, submit a revised name or file an administrative remedy with the Cantonal Department of Economic Affairs; reapply within five working days with a corrected name reservation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening blocked escrow account and payment of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank in Canton Zug (e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or private bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked corporate formation account in the company name, deposit at least CHF 50,000 from founder funds, and obtain a banker's confirmation of the deposit. The account remains blocked until the Commercial Register entry is completed, and the funds must be traceable for capital verification and money-laundering compliance.
required_dossiers: Founder remittance slips or payment confirmation orders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues a KYC or beneficial-ownership query, provide supplementary ownership evidence and source-of-funds explanations; if unresolved, close the draft account and open a new blocked account at another licensed Swiss bank without loss of registration sequence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of incorporation deed and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss notary public (Notariat) in Canton Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange an in-person notarization session for the incorporation deed and full articles of association, including name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, share par value, director appointment, and signature provisions. Ensure founders sign personally or through validly executed powers of attorney and that the notary certifies the share capital declaration.
required_dossiers: Founder passports plus power of attorney if representative is used
Bank confirmation of CHF 50,000 escrow deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies deficiencies, execute a supplemental addendum to the deed on the same session and re-notarize; if statutory content is incomplete, amend the articles and reschedule notarization before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canton Zug Commercial Register Office, online submission portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed, articles of association, board resolution, director signature specimens, and escrow bank confirmation with the Commercial Register. Pay the prescribed registration fee and await the formal entry; the Company acquires legal personality only upon registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, cure all stated defects within the statutory deadline, amend and resubmit the filing; if registration is refused, file an administrative judicial complaint with the cantonal Commercial Register supervisory authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration opening of ordinary bank accounts and corporate seals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank in Canton Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Commercial Register extract, present the certified registration confirmation to release the escrow account and convert it into an operating account. Arrange signature cards, corporate bank mandates, and any required payment card/merchant facility applications for the high-risk nutraceuticals e-commerce activity.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC forms and beneficial ownership statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence for high-risk supplement merchants, supply the operating licence and product compliance certificates; if the bank declines, submit the same dossier to a private Swiss bank or payment processor specialising in high-risk e-commerce.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (Bundesamt für Lebensmittelsicherheit und Veterinärwesen, BLV/FSVO) in cooperation with the Cantonal Chemist of Canton Zug
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Notification for placing food supplements on the Swiss market and establishment permit for online nutraceuticals retail and warehouse operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU/FOEN)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / low-risk commercial warehousing; no full EIA report required unless the site exceeds thresholds under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with the Swiss Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV); the facility is not a significant VOC emitter and must maintain dry commercial storage conditions; all waste handling and disposal must be contracted to licensed operators under the Federal Waste Ordinance (VVEA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification must be obtained from the cantonal fire prevention and building enforcement authority; structural load inspection and occupancy clearance are required for the warehouse; occupational health and safety clearance must be obtained from the cantonal labour inspectorate in accordance with the Swiss Labour Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC) and its SuisTax portal; official e-services at https://www.estv.admin.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident enterprise must register for Swiss VAT under Art. 10 para. 2 lit. b VAT Act if its Swiss-sourced turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year. Registration is made through the SuisTax online portal (or Form 101) with the FTA, providing evidence of the applicant's foreign corporate status, the nature of Swiss supplies, turnover computations, and, if the applicant has no permanent establishment in Switzerland, the appointment of a resident fiscal representative. The issued Swiss VAT number is the UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer) in the format CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx MWST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None materially comparable to US check-the-box. Swiss corporate law imposes an entity-level tax on an Aktiengesellschaft; no pass-through election is available for an AG. Hybrid mismatch restrictions under Swiss tax law (2019 OECD BEPS-aligned amendments) operate as disallowance rules, not elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT; Mehrwertsteuer MWST / taxe sur la valeur ajoutée TVA) administered by the Swiss Federal Tax Administration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Resident businesses: CHF 250,000 annual worldwide turnover (excluding exempt real-estate supplies). Non-resident businesses with no residence or place of business in Switzerland: CHF 100,000 annual taxable turnover derived from Swiss supplies (Art. 10 VAT Act).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory continuous controls (CTC). E-invoicing is voluntary; Swiss QR-bill and e-bill standards are accepted. The law requires invoices to state the supplier's UID MWST number and all Swiss VAT elements; no fiscal API, no digital stamping, and no private-sector e-invoicing mandate exists. Export invoices must be supported by customs export declarations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods qualify for 0% VAT when removed from Switzerland to a foreign destination (export) or transferred as deemed export; services qualify under Art. 23 VAT Act if the beneficiary is resident abroad, provided the place of supply is in Switzerland. The supplier must hold reliable documentary evidence that export has occurred (e.g., customs export record).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration/Ausfuhrzollanmeldung (via Swiss Customs e-dec system)
Transport documents evidencing international carriage (Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR)
Commercial invoice and, where applicable, packing list
Proof of export date and destination; for services, foreign beneficiary and economic activity evidence
Inward remittance certificate or bank transfer evidence (where used for commercial proof; not a statutory VAT requirement)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss VAT export zero-rating is reviewed ex post by the FTA through documentary and customs audits. If export status is not substantiated, the VAT becomes payable at 8.1% together with delinquency interest; a wrongful claim may be treated as tax evasion (Art. 56 VAT Act) and carry fines up to three times the tax evaded and potential criminal sanctions. Reassessments for VAT are generally not time-barred where the taxpayer acted with intent.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB; German: Schweizerische Nationalbank; English: Swiss National Bank, headquartered in Bern and Zurich)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a fully liberalised and convertible currency regime for both the current and capital accounts. The Swiss franc (CHF) is not subject to exchange controls, minimum holding periods, quantitative restrictions, or central bank licensing for cross-border fund movement. Profit repatriation, dividend distributions, shareholder loan servicing, and intra-group treasury flows are legally unrestricted; no SNB approval or declaration of intent is required for cross-border payments. The only frictions are (i) the Swiss 35% withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividend distributions, which may be reduced or eliminated under Switzerland's network of double tax treaties or refunded to qualifying Swiss-resident corporate shareholders; and (ii) Switzerland's implementation of international sanctions, which requires that all cross-border payments and counterparties be screened against SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs), FINMA, OFAC, EU, and UN sanction lists. For e-commerce supply chains sourcing dietary supplements from Asia, the practical constraint is not convertibility but compliance with Swiss food-labelling law, the Therapeutic Products Act, and the counterparty/KYC standards imposed by Swiss banks on high-risk merchandise segments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender, earmarking, or mandatory conversion obligations in Switzerland. Swiss exporters and cross-border e-commerce operators are free to retain 100% of their export and sales receipts in any currency (USD, EUR, CNY, etc.) in Swiss or foreign bank accounts, and may convert those proceeds on the market at any time without SNB permission. The only compulsory reporting is statistical: under the SNB Ordinance on the gathering of statistical data, direct exporters and treasury entities must report aggregate balance-of-payments statistics (customs data for goods, and financial flows over CHF 10 million) at fixed deadlines. There is no minimum conversion ratio, no forced sale into CHF, and no requirement to use a designated state bank.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational CHF/EUR/USD treasury account plus segregated Capital Escrow Account for AG paid-in capital verification
Operational Account and short-term liquidity deposit; can also host the statutory share-capital escrow until reissuance of the capital confirmation
Operational Account for merchant settlement and trade payments
Operational Account with extensive trade-finance desk for pharmaceutical and dietary-supplement cross-border flows

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Cantonale de Genève (BCGE, Quai de l'Ile, Geneva)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and escrow account; suitable for Geneva-based holding and distribution substructure
Private banking vehicle; unsuitable as a primary operating account for high-frequency e-commerce merchant settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability: Low-to-Medium as principal banking rail, but Medium as a secondary receivables-acquirer under FINMA supervision. Full EU/EEA Payment Institution (PSD2) and E-Money Institution passports do NOT automatically extend to Switzerland, which is not an EEA member. For an EU/UK-based EMI to offer professional services to the Swiss AG, it must either rely on a Swiss-regulated discovery-passport arrangement (limited for payment services) or obtain a FinTech Licence under Art. 1b of the Swiss Banking Act as a FINMA-supervised operator of a deposits-holding payment system. The Swiss FinTech licence regime permits interest-free deposits up to CHF 100 million but does not itself authorise lending; additionally, the company is subject to the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG/AMLA) and must be affiliated with a recognised AML self-regulatory body (e.g., VQF or AMLS). For the specific nutraceuticals e-commerce profile, most Swiss Tier-1 banks refuse acquiring for dietary-supplement merchants classified as high risk; therefore the practical blueprint is to onboard a regulated Tier-1 bank for treasury, and to pair it with either (i) a specialised FINMA-licensed FinTech/PSP (operating under an Art. 1b license or a full banking license) for card acquiring, or (ii) a PCI-DSS Level-1 payment orchestration platform with licensed EU acquiring backbone operating per Article 3(b) of the Swiss Payment Services Act (PSA) through an EU agent arrangement. The strictly offshore EMI (e.g., Malta, Lithuania, UK, or US) is legally viable only as a technical gateway if it holds a valid FINMA passport or the Swiss entity completes a fiduciary agency agreement with a Swiss licensed bank; otherwise using an offshore EMI for core CHF liquidity or settlement of trade payables should be treated as a critical regulatory blocker
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a corporate entity engaged in cross-border high-risk e-commerce, Swiss banks applying the CDB 20 (SBA Code of Conduct with regard to client due diligence) and FINMA AML circular 2016/7 generally mandate a physical face-to-face interview for at least one beneficial owner with genuine control (usually the chief executive or a managing director empowered with sole signature authority over the treasury accounts). Remote onboarding is not acceptable as an exclusive pathway for a high-risk merchant: the bank will require an in-branch appointment at the Swiss registered office or at a Swiss notary public, with the physical presence of the signatories and provision of corporate identity documents, board resolutions, and a sanctions-free declaration. Additionally, the bank will conduct a site-visit to the registered office or, if the commercial substance is abroad, to the fulfilment centre; a mere virtual-office presence in Zug or Zurich is an automatic blocker. Where the beneficial owner cannot attend in person due to residence outside Switzerland, Swiss banks may accept a notarised mandate carried out by a sworn attorney-in-fact who appears at the bank, provided the attorney holds a written power of attorney certified by a Swiss notary and the ultimate beneficial owner consents in writing; however, for high-risk corporate clients, key-man physical presence is effectively a non-waivable mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque or multi-layer beneficial-ownership structure above the Swiss AG or nominee shareholders without verifiable ultimate ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete share register (Aktienbuch) with certified copies of shareholder passports; deed of incorporation with notarised statutory reports for the full ownership chain; sworn statement of patrimony; source-of-wealth evidence; a tax-residence certificate for every shareholder owning 10% or more; written confirmation that no nominee, bearer-share, or trustee arrangement conceals a third-party economic interest, or alternatively a fully disclosed FINMA-compliant fiduciary agreement

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry red flag: online dietary-supplement retail and refund-pattern exposure classified as high-risk merchant under Visa VAMP / Mastercard MISP rules due to chargeback risk and pharmaceutical-adjacent product claims
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss food-safety registration confirmation from the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV) or a declaration that the products are Novel Food/Food Supplements under Art. 5 of the Food Supplements Ordinance (SO); Swissmedic eligibility opinion confirming products are not medicinal products within the Therapeutic Products Act; EFSA and/or Swiss phytosanitary documentation; approved product list with INCI and batch-certificates of analysis; quality management certificates (ISO 22000, HACCP, GMP for food production); compliant consumer-labelling files in the target jurisdictions; a clear refund policy with documented chargeback-ratio controls (target below 0.4%)

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspicious cross-border payment pattern: high value card settlement via payment gateways located in tax-neutral or high-exposure jurisdictions, mixed business and personal flows, non-transparent liquidity passing through intermediate PSPs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Master Services Agreements and settlement waterfall schedules between the AG and each PSP/acquirer; six months of merchant settlement history; consolidated market-place statements with a breakdown of gross sales, refunds, chargebacks, and fee structures; a detailed trust-fund arrangement layer (PCI-DSS SAQ-D compliance certificate); first-party issuer encryption (E2EE / tokenisation); a written treasury policy requiring all PSP balances to be swept into the Swiss Tier-1 bank on a T+1 basis; a clean sanctions-screening log covering the full payment flow

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Credibility gap on commercial substance: the Swiss AG lacks a substantive Swiss office, outsourced fulfilment abroad, and the ultimate distributor is bound to a non-EU/OECD supplier
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss commercial lease agreement for the registered operational office; Swiss-registered trademark/IP ownership and royalty/licence agreements; real senior management presence evidenced by social-insurance (AHV) registrations and Swiss payroll records; third-party fulfilment-centre agreements with global track-and-trace; supplier vetting files including GMP inspections and sanitary certificates; product-liability insurance (Swiss insurer) with minimum coverage of CHF 5 million; copies of the General Terms and Conditions and privacy policy as required by the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP)

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Treasury anomaly: shareholders or directors domiciled in sanctions-sensitive jurisdictions, or expected payment routes involving OFAC/EU-sanctioned entities in the pharma/nutraceutical supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions-screen of all shareholders, beneficial owners, suppliers, marketplaces, and payment processors against SECO, EU, OFAC, and UN files; signed Statutory Representation Letter under Swiss criminal law (Art. 309 Swiss Criminal Procedure Code); detailed EBITDA forecast demonstrating legitimate trade volume; confirmation of no crypto or digital-asset settlement with unrestricted anonymity; a sworn declaration of no export to sanctioned states and no use of 'crystal' or high-potency SARMs or other substance-class products subject to the Swiss Narcotics Act

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire-transfer protocol for initial AG financing: (i) equity subscription through a notarised capital-increase deed (Kapitalerhöhung) or formation deed stating a CHF 100,000 minimum nominal capital with at least 20% paid-up; (ii) remittance via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to Switzerland using the payment purpose narrative 'Liberierung Aktienkapital / Equity Contribution – Art. 632 Swiss Code of Obligations' tied to the notarial file number; (iii) the payment should arrive at the Swiss bank's segregated account opened specifically for the capital deposit, and the Swiss bank will issue a 'Bestätigung über die vollständige Liberierung' (blocking confirmation) required for the commercial-register filing; (iv) if the shareholder is outside OECD, an added compliance layer includes a source-of-funds statement from the originating bank, certified by a correspondent bank of a G10 jurisdiction; (v) designating the SWIFT reference with the ISIC tray code '4791' is optional, and the Swiss bank requires the purpose code 'PURPOSE: CAPBS' (Capital BoP supplementary) or the national BoP statistic code for capital formation; (vi) no FX conversion is required at entry since CHF is the functional currency, but upon immediate conversion of foreign-currency funds, the Swiss bank must record the transaction under SNB balance-of-payments statistics; (vii) for shareholder loans, the rail differs slightly: documented subordination agreement to the AG's present and future liabilities, arm's-length interest rates per Finanzierungsfreizügigkeit doctrine, and SAS guidelines to avoid deemed reclassification of the loan into taxable equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103/MT202 for high-value supplier invoices (raw-materials, encapsulation, packaging, freight) with mandatory details: invoices, packing lists, bills of lading/airway bills, and letter-of-credit reference where applicable; settlement cycles of USD/EUR T+0 to T+2 via Swiss banks' correspondent corridors through Chase New York, BNY Mellon, or Deutsche Bank Frankfurt; (2) SEPA Instant Credit / SEPA Credit Transfer for euro-zone supplier invoices under EUR 100,000; (3) Commercial and Standby Letters of Credit (MT700/MT760) issued by the Swiss AG's bank in favour of Asia-Pacific and EU suppliers for bulk purchase of vitamins and nutraceutical premixes, typically 90-day sight or deferred payment, financed against warehouse receipts; (4) documentary collection (D/P and D/A) for over-the-counter pharmacy lines; (5) card-clearing rail for marketplace receivables via Visa NET / Mastercard Switch, with the Swiss AG settling through a registered QSP acquirer (e.g., Barclays, Adyen, Worldline, Checkout.com) and the acquirer disbursing to the Swiss AG's main operating account; (6) FX conversion and hedging overlay: invoice-matching treasury policy requiring FX conversion only at natural hedging gates, with a maximum uncovered USD/EUR/CNY exposure of 20% of projected cash flows; (7) sanctions and export-control screening of each disbursement at the SWIFT level on the ISBP/URR and SECO/EU lists, with trade-finance documents routed through an in-house compliance reviewer before release to the payment instruction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards (plain vanilla CHF/USD, CHF/EUR, CHF/CNY) with settlement in cash between the Swiss AG and a FINMA-licensed counterparty under an ISDA 2002 master agreement with Swiss Schedule; no documentation required from SNB for underlying commercial exposure

FX swaps (swap de change) combining a spot CHF/EUR or CHF/USD transaction with a simultaneous forward reversal, booked under the ISDA 2002 Credit Support Annex to cover working-capital conversion timing

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in KRW, INR, TWD, and offshore CNH for Asian supplier pipelines where the underlying currency is non-clearing or restricted; NDFs must reference the prevailing offshore fixing and evidence the underlying payables invoice to avoid speculation classification

Cross-currency swaps (discrete cross-currency interest-rate swap) between CHF fixed and EUR/USD floating for the financing of inventory and warehouse securitisation, limited to swap tenors not exceeding 12 months and matched to receivable postings

Plain vanilla European-style FX options (collars and strangles) for protection of gross margin on high-season inventory, purchased on a premium-payment basis and limited to notional of not more than 30% of projected quarterly revenue, executed via the bank's electronic trading platform pursuant to FINMA suitability mandates

Commodity-forward-embedded FX hedges for 'from-earth' raw-material purchases (e.g., curcumin, spirulina) where price quotation includes both underlying commodity and FX rate in a single synthetic swap, permitted under the Swiss Financial Services Act if executed by a supervised firm

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and, if applicable, auditor's report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Register of the Canton of registered seat (Handelsregisteramt)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after balance sheet date for shareholder approval; filing with commercial register within 12 months after balance sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties imposed by the cantonal commercial register (up to CHF 5,000); failure to remedy within the statutory deadline may trigger judicial dissolution and strike-off from the commercial register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (federal, cantonal and communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Authority (Kantonale Steuerverwaltung); Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 March to 31 March following the end of the tax year; extensions to June–September commonly granted upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 3%–4% per annum on unpaid taxes; late-filing penalty up to 10% of the assessed tax; intentional non-filing constitutes tax evasion with criminal sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days following the end of each VAT period; annual basis permitted for turnover below CHF 5,000,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 5% per annum; administrative penalty of up to 10% of the evaded tax; repeated non-filing may lead to jeopardy assessment and fines

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory ordinary audit (Art. 727 CO) if the company (a) is listed, or (b) exceeds for two consecutive years two of three thresholds: CHF 20m total assets, CHF 40m turnover, 250 full-time employees. Companies not exceeding these thresholds require limited audit (review) unless the shareholders unanimously waive the audit for companies with fewer than 10 full-time employees (Art. 727a–727b CO).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss GAAP (Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 957 et seq.) for statutory individual accounts; IFRS or another recognised accounting framework is permitted for consolidated reporting or if chosen as statutory framework under applicable law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The board of directors must maintain and update the share register (Aktienbuch) and, where bearer shares exist, the register of beneficial owners. At least once a year, the board must reconcile the register against current ownership and document any share transfers with delivery confirmations; the completed register must be retained at the seat of the company and presented to authorised authorities on demand. No public or governmental annual UBO filing is required in Switzerland, but statutory records must be current at every filing date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholder and board meeting minutes)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal direct tax on net profit after tax (equivalent to 7.83% on pre-tax profit); combined federal plus cantonal plus communal effective rates range from 11.9% (Zug) to 21.6% (Geneva) depending on the canton of domicile; the composite jurisdiction applies a unitary national system with mandatory federal tax uniformity.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation relief under Article 69 DBG: 100% exemption of qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from participations of at least 10% or CHF 1 million market value; patent box relief up to 90% exemption of qualifying IP income; R&D super-deduction of 50% of labour-related R&D costs under the STAF/OASI reform package; notional interest deduction on surplus security equity available in most cantons; holding-company and mixed-company privileged regimes abolished from 1 January 2020 but replaced by the above instruments; no separate approval is required beyond the ordinary return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal and federal corporate income tax return (Steuererklärung für juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales); e-filed through the competent cantonal tax administration's mandatory electronic portal (e.g., the e-tax filing systems of the Canton of Zug and other cantons); the federal share is administered by the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC); supporting schedules for the tax computation of taxable net profit and the taxable equity capital statement must be attached.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (single statutory filing covering both federal and cantonal direct taxes; the tax period corresponds to the statutory business year, normally the calendar year; no quarterly corporate income tax returns are required, but cantons may demand quarterly provisional tax payments by instalment).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by 31 March of the year following the tax period under Article 124 DBG; the cantonal tax authority may grant extensions upon reasoned request, typically to 30 September or, for tax-advisor filings, to 31 December of the assessment year; the federal deadline runs concurrently with the cantonal deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered seat, UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), date of incorporation, commercial register number, legal form AG, and the business purpose including online retail of dietary supplements and nutraceuticals.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the Swiss-registered AG details and, in the shareholders' schedule, the foreign parent, intermediate holding company, and ultimate beneficial owner with foreign addresses and residence country; no foreign company registration is required for a Swiss domestic AG.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section B, Line 2 (Net profit before taxes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net income per audited annual financial statements before corporate taxes, computed per Article 58 DBG on full worldwide income with statutory Swiss accounting and tax-law adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file this return; the AG itself is the taxpayer and must report worldwide income; no reduction is permitted for undistributed reserves except statutory participation relief or patent box deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying dividend and capital-gain income deduction per Article 69 DBG, with a supporting schedule showing the participation percentage, acquisition cost, market value, and the amount of exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Relief is available to the Swiss AG even with non-resident ownership if the 10% or CHF 1 million participation threshold is met; attach the share register and proof of the foreign investee's profit distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable equity capital for cantonal/communal capital tax, based on the Swiss statutory balance sheet with tax-law adjustments including hidden reserves and unrecognised provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident capital contributions must be evidenced by notarised capital increase deeds, bank transfer records, and the share register (Aktienbuch) to prevent recharacterisation as hidden equity distributions subject to 35% withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unilateral relief or treaty credit for foreign-source income per Article 53 DBG, limited to the Swiss effective tax rate on that income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding taxes on royalties, interest, or dividends derived from the cross-border pharmaceutical supplement distribution chain must be evidenced by foreign tax certificates; attach the applicable DTA article and computation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for non-arm's-length transactions with related parties, including hidden profit distributions; separate line for overpriced intercompany purchases, royalties, management fees, and financing charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent groups must attach a transfer pricing documentation index, an arm's-length benchmark study for the e-commerce platform fees, IP royalties, logistics charges, and intercompany loans, and a declaration that prices conform to the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Date, place, taxpayer signature, tax advisor signature, power of attorney, and declaration of completeness and truthfulness; separate section for the election to apply patent box or notional interest deduction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The return must be signed by a director with authority to bind the AG; if no director is resident in Switzerland, the company must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative with service-of-process authority, and the power of attorney must be notarised for foreign signatories.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a procedural fine (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 1,000 under Article 174 DBG, plus equivalent or higher cantonal fines; late-payment interest accrues at 4.5% p.a. from the statutory due date under Article 128 DBG; after a formal reminder and set deadline, continued default triggers a default assessment based on the taxpayer's disclosed base with a one-third surcharge under Article 130 DBG; intentional omission constitutes tax evasion punishable by a penalty of 1x to 3x the evaded tax under Article 175 DBG; directors who caused the non-compliance are personally liable for the assessments and penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% flat Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on gross dividends paid by the Swiss AG, levied under Articles 1 and 13 of the Federal Withholding Tax Act (VStG), irrespective of the shareholder's residence or nationality.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The AG must deduct 35% at the source and remit the amount to the Federal Tax Administration within 30 days of the dividend resolution together with the withholding tax return (Form 103 or the e-tax payment channel). To obtain relief at source (Erlass an der Quelle), an EU/EEA shareholder with a qualifying participation may submit Form 823-A plus a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority before the payment date; non-EU/EEA treaty shareholders must file a refund application on Form 823 with ESTV within three years of the dividend payment date, attaching (i) the TRC covering the payment date, (ii) a beneficial-ownership declaration, (iii) the custodian bank's share-holding confirmation (Form 823-B if applicable), and (iv) a schedule of shares held and dividend amounts; refunds are granted at the applicable treaty rate, typically 0% for qualifying participations of at least 10% and 10-15% for portfolio holdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: no Swiss withholding tax applies to outbound royalty payments to non-residents unless the underlying IP is economically connected to a Swiss permanent establishment or the payment is recharacterised as a constructive dividend; interest: no Swiss withholding tax on ordinary intercompany straight-loan interest at arm's-length rates, whereas interest on Swiss-issued bonds, debentures, or bank-listed money-market instruments is subject to 35% withholding tax; treaty rates under Switzerland's DTA network generally range from 0% to 10% for royalties and 0% to 10% for interest, with domestic law prevailing for non-treaty residents.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Swiss law prescribes no fixed statutory monetary threshold for the Local File or Master File; the Federal Tax Administration and cantonal tax authorities expect full transfer pricing documentation where intragroup transactions with related parties exceed CHF 5 million per transaction category in a given year or where annual turnover exceeds CHF 50 million; Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting is mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least CHF 900 million under Article 129b DBG; the tax authority retains discretion to issue a documentation order in any audit irrespective of entity size.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no Economic Substance Regulations statute of the UAE/Gulf type; however, economic substance is enforced through the place-of-effective-management doctrine (Article 50 DBG), the general anti-abuse rule (Article 21 DBG), the OECD Principal Purpose Test (PPT) implemented via the Multilateral Instrument, and the Federal Withholding Tax Act's anti-avoidance practice for holding companies. To claim treaty benefits, participation relief, or group financing privileges, a Swiss AG must demonstrate real local substance: a physical office, genuine board decision-making in Switzerland documented by minutes, an operational e-commerce platform managed from Swiss premises, adequate payroll and staff, and audited financial statements. A tax-resident shell with solely non-resident beneficial owners, no employees, and no business activity is presumptively abusive and may be disregarded for tax purposes, with profits reattributed to the foreign beneficial owners and treaty access denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion under Federal Direct Tax Law (Steuerhinterziehung)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally false or incomplete tax returns; suppressed revenue from cross-border e-commerce sales of dietary supplements; forged invoices from related party distributors; undisclosed foreign bank accounts of the AG; or wilful omission of taxable income in the online retail business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 175 DBG: penalty of 1x to 3x the evaded tax plus default interest at 4.5% p.a.; qualified tax fraud under Article 186 DBG (use of forged or falsified documents) carries imprisonment up to 3 years or a monetary penalty, with an extended 15-year statute of limitation; cantonal law mirrors federal penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who prepare, sign, or cause false declarations are joint and severally liable for the evaded tax amounts, penalties, and interest; criminal conviction triggers personal fines, economic disqualification, travel bans, and extradition risk; if combined with money laundering, Swiss Criminal Code Articles 305bis and 305ter impose imprisonment up to 5 years and asset freezing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to deduct, remit, or report the 35% Swiss withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; staging dividend flows through low-tax foreign holding companies without substance in order to avoid the 35% levy; or late payment of the withheld amounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 16 VStG: the AG's board is personally liable for the amount of tax not withheld; Article 65 VStG: fine up to CHF 30,000 for procedural violations; default interest at 5% p.a.; the Federal Tax Administration may seize bank accounts and initiate administrative debt collection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the fiscal representative are jointly and severally liable for the unremitted 35% amount as third-party debtors under Article 12 paragraph 5 VStG; wilful non-compliance is a penal offence leading to fines, director disqualification, and potential criminal extradition in cross-border enforcement proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Abusive Tax Structuring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Swiss AG as a letterbox entity: no office, no Swiss employees, all administration conducted abroad, passive income booked in Switzerland solely to obtain treaty benefits and participation relief for a cross-border nutraceuticals group where IP ownership and decision-making reside outside Switzerland.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 21 DBG (Steuerumgehung) permits the tax authority to disregard the corporate vehicle; profits are reattributed to the foreign beneficial owners; treaty relief is denied under the OECD Principal Purpose Test; back taxes and interest are assessed for the full statutory period (10 years for recklessness, 15 years for fraud); criminal referral for qualified tax evasion is possible.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors who knowingly lend their titles without exercising genuine control are personally liable for restitution of the tax advantages, including the 35% withholding tax; they may be prosecuted for aiding and abetting evasion, subjected to Schengen-wide travel bans, and disqualified from serving as directors in any Swiss company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Adjustment and Constructive Dividend
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Unjustified mark-ups on intercompany e-commerce platform fees; inflated royalties for marketing intangibles paid to a related foreign IP mailbox company; intercompany loans with interest rates outside the arm's-length range; year-end round-trip transactions to shift profit out of Switzerland without economic justification or documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation of the excess payment as a hidden profit distribution (verdeckte Gewinnausschüttung): the adjustment is added to taxable profit, subject to the 35% Swiss withholding tax if the shareholder is non-resident, plus a penalty of 1x to 3x of the underpaid tax under Article 175 DBG; failure to produce documentation triggers a one-third assessment surcharge under Article 130 DBG.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed the non-arm's-length contracts are jointly liable for the assessed withholding tax under Article 16 VStG, interest, and penalties; arrangements that prejudice creditor rights or the tax authority expose directors to criminal liability for fraudulent bankruptcy or asset stripping under Swiss Criminal Code Articles 163 and 164, carrying imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the high-risk dietary supplement merchant without the required regulatory licence; accepting credit-card payments through shell or unlicensed payment processors; commingling corporate funds with crypto assets of the beneficial owner; failing to identify customers or the origin of funds; or making false customs declarations for unregistered supplements shipped into the EU.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG) and Swiss Criminal Code Article 305bis (money laundering) are punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine; participation in a criminal organisation raises the minimum term; the Therapeutic Products Act (HMG Article 86) imposes fines up to CHF 50,000 with product seizure; payment processors may terminate high-risk merchant accounts, and financial intermediaries must file suspicious transaction reports.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with knowledge or suspicion of laundering are criminally liable in personam and subject to asset confiscation, travel bans, and extradition; the corporate veil is pierced for restitution of illicit proceeds under Swiss Criminal Code Articles 70 to 73; the company's bank accounts are frozen and the directors may be banned from managing any Swiss business for up to 10 years.
